commit_message: PR #2829: archive_write_shar_header: free shar->last_dir before replacement
vulnerability_type: Memory leak in archive_write_shar_header due to missing free of shar->last_dir before reassignment
poc_sketch: Repeatedly create shar archives with different directory entries to trigger the header code path where last_dir gets replaced without being freed, causing unbounded memory consumption and potential denial of service
backport_notes: Single line addition: free(shar->last_dir) before the pointer reassignment. The surrounding context (shar_quote, archive_strcat, conditional block) is stable across versions. No dependencies on newer APIs or structural changes.
logical_survival: The shar format writer is mature, stable core code with minimal churn, and the patch is a pure memory-management fix decoupled from any version-specific features or API changes.
ubuntu_2604_evidence: Manual backport / Debian-layer patch (author: kientzle@acm.org). upstream: Merge pull request #2829 from AZero13/leak-shar
_cot_rationale: The patch adds a single free(shar->last_dir) call before the pointer is reassigned at line ~245. This is a classic memory leak where the old string allocation is orphaned when last_dir is updated with a new directory path. Ubuntu 24.04 ships libarchive 3.7.2 which predates the fix (commit 6f9adc5d present in 3.8.5). The vulnerable code pattern - allocating a string, storing it in shar->last_dir, then later overwriting that pointer without freeing - is present in the 24.04 version. The shar writer is stable, rarely-modified code with no structural dependencies on newer libarchive internals. The fix is a textbook one-line cherry-pick with no adaptation needed.

commit_message: PR #2813: We copy from p, not p + module_len
vulnerability_type: Incorrect pointer arithmetic in memcpy overwrites safety prefix instead of appending option string
poc_sketch: Set LIBARCHIVE_WRITER_OPTIONS or LIBARCHIVE_READER_OPTIONS environment variable to a crafted options string; the IGNORE_WRONG_MODULE_NAME prefix is immediately overwritten by memcpy(p, ...) instead of being preserved via memcpy(p + module_len, ...), defeating the intended option-filtering safety mechanism and leaving uninitialized heap data in the tail of the allocated buffer
backport_notes: Two one-line changes: add '+ module_len' to the destination pointer in two memcpy calls (lines 158 and 191); no surrounding code changes needed, no dependency on newer APIs or structures
logical_survival: The vulnerable code is simple, stable environment-variable option-handling utility code that has not been restructured across versions; the fix is a pure pointer-arithmetic correction completely decoupled from any version-specific features.
ubuntu_2604_evidence: Manual backport / Debian-layer patch (author: martin@matuska.de). upstream: Merge pull request #2813 from AZero13/memcpy
_cot_rationale: Examining the 24.04 source at lines 157-158 (set_writer_options) and 190-191 (set_reader_options), both memcpy calls use 'p' as destination instead of 'p + module_len', confirming the bug matches the upstream description exactly. The buffer is malloc'd as module_len + opt_len, IGNORE_WRONG_MODULE_NAME is correctly copied first, but then the second memcpy overwrites offset 0 instead of offset module_len — destroying the prefix and leaving opt_len through module_len+opt_len-1 as residual heap data. The upstream fix (commit c8ea1e5) changes exactly two lines, adding '+ module_len' to each destination pointer. The 24.04 code structure is identical to the patched version's context, so cherry-pick applies cleanly. Severity is MEDIUM: this is primarily a logic/safety-mechanism bypass rather than direct memory corruption, though it could expose heap contents to archive option parsing in edge cases.

The MEDIUM vulnerability (Incorrect pointer arithmetic in memcpy overwrites safety prefix instead of appen) should be absent from the Noble changelog entirely.

commit_message: PR #2768: Fix for an out-of-bounds buffer overrun when using p[H_LEVEL_OFFSET]
vulnerability_type: Out-of-bounds buffer read in LHA header parsing via unchecked p[H_LEVEL_OFFSET] access
poc_sketch: Craft a malicious LHA archive with a truncated or malformed header such that the buffer p is too short to safely access offset H_LEVEL_OFFSET, triggering an out-of-bounds read when the condition p[H_LEVEL_OFFSET] == 0 is evaluated during archive_read_format_lha_read_header
backport_notes: Single-line substitution replacing direct buffer access p[H_LEVEL_OFFSET] with already-parsed lha->level field; only prerequisite is confirming lha->level is populated before this code point, which it is from prior header parsing in lha_read_file_header_0/1
logical_survival: The LHA format reader is mature, stable core code that rarely undergoes structural changes, and the patch is fully decoupled from any version-specific API or feature—it simply uses a pre-existing struct field instead of a raw buffer dereference.

Ubuntu 24.04 ships libarchive 3.7.2-2 which predates this fix. The vulnerable line exists in archive_read_format_lha_read_header(), the main header parsing path for LHA archives. Since lha->level is parsed and stored earlier in the header reading sequence (via lha_read_file_header_0), the replacement is safe and correct. The code surrounding this line has not changed between 3.7.2 and 3.8.5, making this a clean one-line cherry-pick with zero context adaptation needed. The vulnerability is HIGH severity because it involves memory corruption (OOB read) in a library that processes untrusted input (archive files), reachable via any application that uses libarchive to open LHA files (e.g., file-roller, 7z, bsdtar).

commit_message: PR #2737: Fix an infinite loop when parsing `V` headers
vulnerability_type: Infinite loop when parsing tar 'V' (volume) headers due to missing negative size check and unchecked consume failures
poc_sketch: Craft a tar archive with a 'V' header containing a negative size field. When libarchive processes this, header_volume fails to reject the negative size, leading to an infinite loop in the tar_read_header retry loop as tar_flush_unconsumed cannot make forward progress and no error is propagated.
backport_notes: The patch changes tar_flush_unconsumed from void to int and requires updating all ~10 call sites to check the return value. The core fix (size < 0 check in header_volume) is a one-liner. The mechanical changes to propagate errors are straightforward but require careful attention to all call sites in the 3.7.2 source.
logical_survival: The tar header parsing code is stable core infrastructure that rarely undergoes structural changes; the patch is purely algorithmic (adding error propagation and a bounds check) and completely decoupled from any version-specific API or feature additions.
ubuntu_2604_evidence: Manual backport / Debian-layer patch (author: kientzle@acm.org). upstream: Merge pull request #2737 from kientzle/kientzle-volume-header-overflow
_cot_rationale: 1. The 24.04 source (v3.7.2) shows tar_flush_unconsumed with void return type at line 231, confirming the vulnerable code pattern exists. 2. The patch's primary fix is adding 'size < 0' validation in header_volume and making tar_flush_unconsumed propagate __archive_read_consume failures - both generic logic fixes. 3. The infinite loop is triggered by negative size in V headers where the void function cannot signal failure, causing tar_read_header's while(1) loop to retry indefinitely. 4. Backport requires changing one function signature and mechanically updating ~10 call sites with error checks - no structural refactoring needed. 5. This is core tar parsing logic common across all versions, making it highly likely the vulnerable pattern survived intact in 24.04.

commit_message: PR #2729: Don't leak memory on fatal error
vulnerability_type: memory leak of write filter state and buffer on fatal error paths
poc_sketch: An attacker crafts an archive that triggers a fatal write error (e.g., via client_opener returning failure, or format_write_data returning ARCHIVE_FATAL). The archive_write_client_close may not execute its cleanup path, and archive_write_client_free in 3.7.2 lacks the free(state->buffer)/free(state) calls, leaking the allocated state and buffer each time such an archive is processed.
backport_notes: The core fix moves free(state->buffer)/free(state) from archive_write_client_close into archive_write_client_free, and removes the redundant cleanup in archive_write_client_open's error path. The _archive_write_finish_entry and _archive_write_data hunks require ARCHIVE_STATE_FATAL to exist in 3.7.2; if not present, a #define or minor adaptation is needed. The bzip2 hunk is independent and straightforward.
logical_survival: The vulnerable code resides in the core archive_write.c write-filter lifecycle (open/close/free) which is fundamental infrastructure unlikely to be restructured across minor versions; the patch is decoupled from version-specific features and addresses a generic memory-management lifecycle bug.
ubuntu_2604_evidence: Manual backport / Debian-layer patch (author: kientzle@acm.org). upstream: Merge pull request #2729 from KlaraSystems/des/leak-on-fatal
_cot_rationale: In 3.7.2, archive_write_client_free() does not free state->buffer or state itself — those are only freed in archive_write_client_close(). If a fatal error prevents close from running its full cleanup, or if the error occurs in client_opener (where open() does free on failure but then returns ARCHIVE_FATAL, potentially skipping the later free path), memory is leaked. The upstream patch (1) moves the free(state->buffer)/free(state) into archive_write_client_free so cleanup is always reached, (2) removes the now-redundant frees from close and open's error path, and (3) properly transitions to ARCHIVE_STATE_FATAL so subsequent operations don't attempt to use freed state. The code structure in 3.7.2 matches the pre-patch state exactly, confirming the vulnerability exists. Backport is easy because the changes are confined to well-scoped functions with no dependencies on new APIs.

poc_sketch: Craft a malformed JP2 file with truncated or oversized code-block segment data that triggers partial_buffer path in opj_t2_read_packet_data; the codeblock's numchunks is zeroed but opj_t1_decode_cblk still attempts to access chunk data via mustuse_cblkdatabuffer path without checking numchunks > 0, causing heap-buffer-overflow read
backport_notes: Three files need changes: (1) tcd.h requires adding OPJ_BOOL corrupted field to opj_tcd_cblk_dec_t struct, (2) t1.c needs two small additions - early return on cblk->corrupted and guarding the mustuse_cblkdatabuffer condition with numchunks > 0, (3) t2.c needs restructuring of the error handling loop to set corrupted flag and simplified break logic. The t2.c changes are the most involved due to loop restructuring but the surrounding context in 2.5.0 should match closely.

Since 2.5.0 has none of these, the vulnerability is confirmed present. vulnerability_type: EmbedStream getChars() buffer over-read and state confusion via rewind/restore misuse
poc_sketch: Craft a PDF with an inline image that triggers the PSOutputDev::doImageL1Sep or ImageOutputDev::writeImage code paths. The inline image causes EmbedStream::rewind() to be called after initial read, then EmbedStream::getChars() is invoked during replay mode. Due to the bug, memcpy reads from bufData[0] instead of bufData[bufPos], bufPos is never incremented, and the return value is the remaining buffer length rather than actual bytes copied — leading to memory corruption and potential code execution.
backport_notes: The patch spans 4 files (Stream.h, Stream.cc, PSOutputDev.cc, ImageOutputDev.cc). Key obstacles: (1) must remove rewind()/restore() methods and the 'record' member variable, (2) must fix getChars() memcpy source from bufData to &bufData[bufPos] and add bufPos increment, (3) must rework reset() to set replay=true for reusable streams, (4) must update all callers (PSOutputDev, ImageOutputDev) to use reset() instead of rewind()/restore(). The changes are logically coherent but require verifying no other callers of rewind()/restore() exist in 24.02.0.
logical_survival: The EmbedStream class is core infrastructure in poppler's stream handling that is unlikely to have been restructured between minor versions, and the patch fixes generic algorithmic bugs (wrong memcpy offset, missing bufPos increment, broken record/replay state machine) that are fully decoupled from any version-specific API features.
ubuntu_2604_evidence: Reachable from upstream tag poppler-26.01.0; arrived via natural version import. upstream: Remove EmbedStream rewind and restore
_cot_rationale: Ubuntu 24.04 ships poppler 24.02.0 which still has the buggy rewind()/restore() pattern and the getChars() buffer handling bugs. The critical bugs are: (1) memcpy uses bufData instead of &bufData[bufPos] causing reads from wrong offset, (2) bufPos is never incremented causing infinite replay of same data, (3) return value is remaining length not bytes copied causing callers to misinterpret buffer contents.
